hook: Your vehicle number could reveal your *name, address and phone* for ₹5. Govt orders an audit
tldr: The road transport ministry asked CERT-In to forensically audit the VAHAN, SARATHI, e-Challan and PUCC portals after reports that vehicle owners' details were being sold online, some for as little as ₹5.

beats.what: MoRTH ordered a CERT-In security audit of four portals that hold vehicle and licence data.
beats.why: Security firm Cyderes found apps and Telegram channels selling owners' personal data. Give a registration number and you get the owner's name, father's name, address, mobile number and licence details.
beats.care: Your RC and licence data sit on these portals. Be wary of calls or messages that quote your vehicle details, and never share OTPs.

cards.body: VAHAN holds vehicle registrations, SARATHI driving licences, e-Challan traffic fines and PUCC pollution certificates. Between them, that's most of India's drivers.

cards.q: Have you got a spam or scam call that knew your vehicle details?

cards.why: VAHAN is registrations, SARATHI licences, e-Challan fines, PUCC pollution certificates.

viz.l: price some sellers charged for a vehicle owner's details
government portals ordered for a security audit

learn.t: CERT-In (the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team) is the national agency that responds to cyber incidents and audits government systems.

watch: The audit's findings, and whether the portals limit what a number-plate search shows.
